title: Mitchell and Phillips bat out the last day as New Zealand draw Wellington Test against India
dek: India's record 720 for nine was not enough: New Zealand batted 120 overs to finish on 239 for five. Henry Nicholls was player of the match, and the second Test starts in Christchurch on 27 November.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The first Test between New Zealand and India in Wellington ended in a draw on Monday, after Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips batted through most of the final two sessions to deny India the eight wickets they needed. New Zealand finished their second innings on 239 for five from 120 overs, 113 runs behind, and the captains shook hands with less than an hour left, according to reports.

Mitchell was unbeaten on 49 off 186 balls and Phillips on 26 off 126. Both teams take four points in the World Test Championship, according to reports. India had declared on Sunday at 720 for nine, the highest total in any Test in New Zealand. Henry Nicholls, whose unbeaten 175 rescued New Zealand from 70 for five in the first innings, was named player of the match.

## The final day

New Zealand resumed at 119 for two on a pitch that offered little to the bowlers. Washington Sundar broke the third-wicket stand when Devon Conway, who had batted for 165 balls, edged to Rishabh Pant for 65. Prasidh Krishna then had Rachin Ravindra caught by KL Rahul for 37, leaving New Zealand at 139 for four, according to reports.

Anshul Kamboj removed Tom Blundell for 15 in the 77th over, caught behind by Pant after India reviewed and edge-detection technology showed a faint touch, which made it 176 for five. That was India's last success. Mitchell and Phillips, who had added 216 for the sixth wicket with Nicholls in the first innings, saw New Zealand to tea at 206 for five, and India turned to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Dhruv Jurel and Devdutt Padikkal as occasional bowlers without a breakthrough, according to reports.

## How the match unfolded

New Zealand made 368 in their first innings, built on Nicholls's 175 not out and Phillips's 118 after the top order collapsed. India replied with 720 for nine declared, with six batters passing fifty: Rahul (136), Pant (128), Shubman Gill (98), Jaiswal (85), Padikkal (80) and Jurel (78).

That total beat New Zealand's 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019 as the highest Test score made in the country, and is India's third-highest in Tests. But India's bowlers took only 15 wickets in the match on a surface on which batting became easier rather than harder.

> "For us to get a draw from where we were was a pleasing result." — Henry Nicholls, after the match

Nicholls said both teams "gave it everything" in what he called "an attritional test", according to reports. Gill, asked about his bowling options, said he hoped for "a bit more help" from the pitch in the next match, according to reports.

## What happens next

The second and final Test of the series begins at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Friday, 27 November, according to reports. With the series level at 0-0, a result there will decide it. Nicholls said he expected the Christchurch pitch to have "some grass and pace", which would bring India's fast bowlers more into the game.
